title: Alert hypothesis catalog and postmortem notebook seeder
creator: Kai Thompson
description: Build a service that collects relevant traces, metrics and log snippets for a triggered PagerDuty incident, synthesizes a prioritized set of root-cause hypotheses, and seeds a postmortem notebook (Markdown + time-ordered timeline + investigation checklist) into the incident Slack thread and the postmortem workspace.
background: On-call engineers spend large fractions of time assembling evidence after an alert — gathering correlated traces, pulling metric queries, and copying log excerpts into a postmortem. We already have tracing hooks and metric pipelines, but there is no standardized automation to assemble candidate causes or a notebook skeleton to accelerate RCA. This ticket prototypes an automated hypothesis generator and notebook seeder that integrates with PD incidents and Slack channels.
goals: When a PagerDuty incident is created, automatically gather the top 3 correlated traces and the 5 highest-impact metric series within the incident window.
Generate 2-4 concise root-cause hypotheses with supporting evidence links (trace IDs, metric charts, log snippets).
Post a seeded postmortem notebook to the incident Slack thread and create a draft postmortem doc in the postmortem workspace with a clickable checklist for investigators.
Provide an opt-out toggle per-service and respect PII retention policies in log snippets.
scope: Integrate with PagerDuty incidents and the existing trace ingest hooks (trace-sampler v2).
Leverage existing metrics pipeline queries in Prometheus/Signalflow and dashboards for chart links.
Create a lightweight notebook template and Slack message composer that can be reviewed/edited by the on-call.
out_of_scope: Full NLP postmortem writing (we will provide hypotheses only, not final narrative).
Automatic remediation or rollback actions (only suggestions).
Deep integration with external compliance ticketing beyond creating the draft doc link.
technical_approach: On PD trigger: collect incident metadata -> call trace-harvest microservice to fetch top-k spans by error-rate and latency anomaly score -> run candidate-scorer (heuristic + small TF model trained on historical postmortems) to produce ranked hypotheses -> build notebook: header, timeline bullets (from trace spans & metric change points), evidence attachments (trace links, chart links, scrubbed log snippets) -> post to slack thread and create draft in /docs/postmortems/automated/. The trace-harvest service will use sampling heuristics to limit noise and will redact known PII tokens via the log-scrubber lambda.
acceptance_criteria: For a synthetic PD incident (test harness), the service returns a seeded notebook with at least 1 hypothesis and 1 trace link 95% of the time.
Slack message includes notebook link and a single-click 'Accept draft' action that copies the draft to the official postmortem repo.
Opt-out toggle respected: incidents for services with opt-out label do not trigger automation.
Automated scrubber removes email addresses and long UUIDs from log snippets in >= 99% of test cases.

rollout_plan: Alpha: opt-in for core infra and runtime teams (2 weeks) - manual review required.
Beta: enable for 20% of incidents for non-prod services (4 weeks) - monitor false-positive hypotheses.
GA: default enabled with per-service opt-out toggle after security signoff and telemetry SLOs met.
monitoring_signals: Feedback_accept_rate (percent of seeded notebooks accepted by oncall)
risks: Overconfident hypotheses leading to biased RCA — mitigate by surfacing confidence and requiring human acceptance.
PII leakage in log snippets — mitigated via log-scrubber and security review.
Model drift for hypothesis scorer as product evolves — monitor feedback_accept_rate and retrain periodically.
test_plan: Unit tests for trace-harvest sampling heuristics and scorer logic.
Integration tests: PD webhook -> trace-harvest -> notebook creation -> Slack post in staging.
Privacy fuzz tests with synthetic PII to validate scrubber rules.
Load test: simulate 200 incidents/hour to validate time_to_notebook_post and trace-harvest scaling.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on quality of evidence assembly and the human-in-the-loop flow. Future follow-ups may add richer NLP summarization and cross-incident similarity searches. Keep the initial scope small to get rapid feedback from oncall engineers.
